items.title: Prove or refute by execution that a hand-edited init-check.json passes the gate unchanged
items.context: Repro-first, and note the corrected premise: signInitCheck never takes agentResults as input, so the test is NOT the discarded draft's two-step 'tamper then re-sign' sequence. Test the one-step claim: in an isolated fixture (never a real story), edit agentResults directly, make NO init_check_set call, then check whether _hash still validates and whether the INIT->INIT_CHECK guard accepts it. Record the observed outcome even if it refutes the premise; a refutation re-scopes items 2-6 rather than being a failure. Probe the fallback-block-drop separately, checking it is lost after the FIRST ordinary call rather than when the attestationMode label flips.
items.userSees: node packages/main/tests/red/<artifact>.mjs prints one line per claim with RED/CONTROL-OK, ends with a RED count, and exits non-zero while the defect stands.

happy.desc: The artifact reproduces the PLAN probe: injected agentResults advances the gate with zero init_check_set calls

verification.selector: the gate ACCEPTS hand-injected reviewer coverage

edge.desc: The artifact also covers the issues field (erasing a recorded critical still advances), so a partial fix cannot turn it green

verification.selector: erasing a recorded blocking-severity issue leaves the file signature-VALID

adversarial.desc: It carries a SIGNATURE control (in-domain title edit must be rejected). If that control fails the run reports BROKEN and draws no conclusion, so a dead signature check cannot masquerade as this defect

verification.selector: SIGNATURE CONTROL: the gate REFUSES that in-domain edit as tampering

items.title: Bind agentResults and issues into the signature domain
items.context: signInitCheck at core/init-check-gate.ts:133-143 and recomputeInitCheckHash at :133-172. Both fields must be covered; fixing agentResults alone leaves an equivalent hole because the same edit can erase a recorded critical issue. Handle all six on-disk shapes (canonical pair, koala pair, two distinct @fallback pairs, three-entry historical-actor files, and files with no agentResults where initCheckAgentResults synthesizes from top-level fields). Decide explicitly what an absent field hashes to. CONDITIONAL ON CHK-001: if CHK-001's execution refutes the premise, re-scope this item before doing any of it rather than executing it as written.

verificationEvidence.note: Waiver for the PIN, not for the property. The property is still mechanically proven: red-b8df9-init-check-verdict-signature.mjs is registered NON-OPTIONAL in lattice.config.json, runs on every validate, and reports 0 RED across 24 rows - rows B1/B2/B3 are exactly this intent. What broke is the pinned selector string. CHK-003 legitimately extended that artifact final conclusion line, so the pinned text "GREEN: both verdict fields are inside the signature domain." (ending in a period) no longer matches verbatim; live output now reads "...signature domain, and the carry-forward...". Verified by execution: grep -F of the pinned string against live output fails. The command+selector pin is immutable on first selector-bearing write, so this cannot be re-pinned and the evidence cannot be re-earned as recorded. LESSON, recorded because the rule I gave was insufficient: I instructed implementers to use MARKER NAMES rather than literal counts as selectors, and this selector obeyed that rule and still broke. The stronger rule is that a selector must be pinned to something no LATER work will legitimately reword - a stable row identifier such as B1 or a machine token, never a prose conclusion sentence, however marker-like it reads. Filed by the test-coverage lane as B-8df9:F-006.

items.title: Verify _hash before trusting previous.agentResults on read
items.context: store.readInitCheck (core/store.ts:566-572) is a bare readJson; the carry-forward at handlers/init-check.ts:138-142 trusts it. This does not cause the gate bypass but does admit data no caller wrote into a subsequently re-signed file. Decide what happens on mismatch: refusing to carry forward is not the same as refusing to read, and that difference decides whether the audit-only majority of the corpus becomes unreadable. CONDITIONAL ON CHK-001: if CHK-001's execution refutes the premise, re-scope this item before doing any of it rather than executing it as written.
items.userSees: A story whose init-check.json has a corrupted _hash reports the corruption by name rather than silently carrying the unverified records forward.

happy.desc: A _hash mismatch on read refuses to carry previous.agentResults forward

edge.desc: Reading a historical file with a legacy hash still RENDERS (story_get / audit paths work); refusing to trust is not refusing to read

adversarial.desc: A file whose _hash was recomputed by an attacker over tampered content is still refused, because the domain now covers the tampered fields

items.title: Preserve the fallback audit block across the merge
items.context: handlers/init-check.ts:144-152 constructs the output without the fallback block written by init_check_repair (reason/actor/session/headHash). It is lost after the first ordinary call, before the initCheckAttestationMode label flips, so the durable evidence of a human attestation disappears earlier than the label advertising it. Preserve it and cover the transition with a test. CONDITIONAL ON CHK-001: if CHK-001's execution refutes the premise, re-scope this item before doing any of it rather than executing it as written.
items.userSees: After a manual init_check_repair, an ordinary init_check_set no longer erases the fallback block; story_get still reports initCheckAttestation: fallback.

happy.desc: An ordinary init_check_set following init_check_repair preserves the fallback block (reason/actor/session/headHash)

edge.desc: initCheckAttestation stays 'fallback' across the first ordinary call, where today the block is dropped one call before the label flips

adversarial.desc: The preserved block cannot be forged into existence by an ordinary call on a story that never ran init_check_repair

ORIGINAL WAIVER TEXT, PRESERVED VERBATIM (this row previously held it; my first correction attempt overwrote it, which I did not intend and have now undone by restoring it here):

"CHK-004 withdrawn by user decision SD-7319de10 (scope-shrinkage-decision.json, userConfirmed=true). No work was done, so no evidence exists. THIS WAIVER IS A FRAMEWORK GAP, NOT A DISPOSITION. The withdrawal is a recorded fact, but the framework cannot read it: scope_shrinkage_decision_set left AB-002 still listing these three intents, whole-binding withdrawal would have dropped delivered CHK-003 coverage, and proofstory_contract_set is refused in REVIEW. A user-approved withdrawal has no mechanical completion path, so this waiver is prose standing where proof should be. Filed as a framework defect; do not read it as evidence."

CORRECTION APPENDED 2026-08-19. The waiver above was accurate when written on 2026-08-03. Its central claim - "A user-approved withdrawal has no mechanical completion path" - IS NO LONGER TRUE. Story B-45a5, merged to main on 2026-08-19, wired decision-backed item-level withdrawal into both REVIEW-path gates: withdrawnItemIntentRefs (core/proofstory.ts:1672, consumed at :2166) subtracts a withdrawn item's intent refs before evaluateReviewCompleteness runs its coverage loop, and checkDispatchEvidence (handlers/validate-channel.ts:305) routes withdrawn items into a third bucket keyed on withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom(decision). Verified live on this story after merging main: validate --channel prints "withdrawn (SD-7319de10): CHK-004" on its own line, absent from the Covered list; proofstory_review_completeness_check reports Gaps 0 with CHK-004's intent refs removed from the required set entirely. Three reviewer lanes independently traced the code and confirmed the gates pass BECAUSE of the withdrawal, never by consulting these waiver rows.

SCOPE OF THAT FIX, stated precisely so this correction does not overclaim: B-45a5 wired the two REVIEW-path gates only. It did NOT make the codebase uniformly decision-backed; core/verification.ts:212 still performs a bare status-string skip on a DONE-blocking path, disclosed and knowingly out of scope there.

The two sibling waiver rows on CHK-004:edge:0 and CHK-004:adversarial:0 carry the same now-superseded claim and this correction covers them too.

items.title: Choose and justify the migration position for the existing corpus
items.context: Re-derive the counts first; do not trust the background's figures. Structure of the argument: only files whose owning story is in INIT are operationally gated (canEnterInitCheckGuard early-returns otherwise, core/machine.ts:440) - at the measured commit that was 1 of 637 - so the real choice is one operational break versus roughly 636 audit-replay breaks. Critically, about 195 of 637 files carry a registry-invalid actor, overwhelmingly the pre-rename koala-review-story-init (zero occurrences in AGENT_DISPATCH_REGISTRY), so re-signing the corpus by routing through the handler is not implementable and any design assuming it is must be rejected. CONDITIONAL ON CHK-001: if CHK-001's execution refutes the premise, re-scope this item before doing any of it rather than executing it as written.
items.userSees: The chosen migration position and its audit-replay consequence are stated in the decision record, with counts re-derived rather than copied.

happy.desc: Counts are re-derived at implementation time rather than copied from the background, and the position names what breaks

edge.desc: The single INIT-phase story is identified by id before landing, and its recorded actors are confirmed still registry-valid

adversarial.desc: The position explicitly rejects any design that assumes the corpus can be re-signed through the handler, since ~195 files carry registry-invalid actors
